This is the authoritative source for polishType and expectedFeatures — NOT vision inference, which got 5 of these 10 types wrong (both thermals read as 'glitter', a magnetic as 'multichrome', two clear-base toppers as 'linear_holo'/'crelly'). vendorDescription is quoted verbatim; the structured fields below it are a reading of that text, so correct the structure rather than the quote if they disagree.

Once You See It._finishNote: Aurora shimmer TRAVELS (green->blue / red->orange) but that is a travelling shimmer, recorded in shimmerFlashColors. It is NOT a multichrome body; tagging it multichrome injects contradictory baseColor guidance.

I Found A Place.uniqueKey: lime green magnetic band over a SHEER TEAL base; aurora shimmer TRAVELS red->orange

_readingRule.title: ON A 'PACKED WITH' POLISH, THE FRAME-DOMINANT COLOUR IS THE SHIMMER, NOT THE BASE
_readingRule.evidence: Owner-identified four Doseoflolade bursts on 2026-08-22. In every case the assistant and the model had named the shade after its shimmer: 'blue' frames were mulberry-based Keep Doubting; 'teal-green' frames were indigo-based What Could Possibly Go Wrong?; 'mulberry/pink' frames were murky-teal-based Fear What You Will Become. Three for three, the same direction of error.
_readingRule.consequence: Any instruction to read the base from the flattest, most face-on, or largest-area patch is WRONG for these polishes - that is exactly where the shimmer fires hardest. The base must be read where the shimmer is NOT firing.

_readingNotes: Frames that read BLUE were "deep mulberry base, packed with BLUE shimmer" (Keep Doubting) — not a blue-based shade.
Frames that read TEAL-GREEN were "deep indigo base, packed with GREEN TO BLUE shimmer" (What Could Possibly Go Wrong?) — not a teal-based shade.
Frames that read MULBERRY/PINK were "murky teal base, packed with MAGENTA TO ORANGE shimmer" (Fear What You Will Become) — not a mulberry-based shade.
Three for three, the obvious reading was wrong in the same direction: the frame was named after its shimmer.
Two frames of a clear blue-flake shade worn over a purple polish were called a purple thermal, because the purple underneath was read as the shade.
